blocks.explanation:
\(\tan^2 x\) has no direct integral, but \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\).
Plan: split into \(\int x\sec^2 x\,dx - \int x\,dx\); do the first by parts (as Example 31).
steps:
Given: \(\int x\tan^2 x\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: use \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\); then integration by parts with \(x\) first and \(\sec^2 x\) second.

Use the identity
\[\int x(\sec^2 x - 1)\,dx\]
\[= \int x\sec^2 x\,dx - \int x\,dx\]
Why: \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\).

Parts on the first integral
\[\int x\sec^2 x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx\]
\[= x\tan x - \ln|\sec x|\]
Why: \(\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x\), \(\int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x|\).

Combine
\[= x\tan x - \ln|\sec x| - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + c\]
Why: \(\int x\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = \tan x + x\sec^2 x - \tan x - x\]
\[= x(\sec^2 x - 1) = x\tan^2 x\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln|\sec x| = \tan x\).
